title: The augmentation cone lies in the subcategory generated by localized modules
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with its ordinary derived category on the one-object bottom site [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal, and let $(K,\epsilon_K)$ satisfy the ordered localization model predicate [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data] for $I$. Let $P$ be a strictly full triangulated subcategory of that derived category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose that $Q(M[0])$ belongs to $P$ whenever $M$ is a module sheaf and multiplication by some element $s\in I$ on its value at the unique object is bijective. Then $Q(\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_K))$ belongs to $P$. No source complex, orthogonality assumption, retract closure or K-flatness is required.

source.place: Tag 0A6R, lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint: the positive localization terms of the augmentation cone and finite degree filtration

proof.text: Choose r and f:Fin r -> A spanning I by finite generation, and unpack the ordered augmented model (C,a,e0,e,alpha). The degree-zero augmentation is an isomorphism: its section map after the canonical single-term identification is exactly the linear equivalence e0. Evaluation at the unique object detects isomorphisms, as verified explicitly by extending a linear inverse to a sheaf morphism. In every other degree the target of a is zero. Therefore a is degreewise epi, hence epi.

For q>=0 the term C^(q+1) is linearly isomorphic on sections to the product over increasing embeddings t:Fin(q+1) -> Fin r of A[1/g_t], where g_t is the product of f(t i). Each g_t belongs to I: f(t 0) belongs to the spanning ideal and divides g_t. Its image in its away localization is a unit, so multiplication by g_t is bijective. Apply hP to each corresponding constant module sheaf. The composite of the existing additive constant-module functor, single in degree zero, and Q is additive and preserves finite products. The concrete module-product isomorphism and the linear equivalence e therefore give P(Q(C^(q+1)[0])). Only the constant-module construction is used from the Godement module; no Godement model or resolution theorem is used.

Use the categorical kernel B=ker(a), which is a uniquely determined limit and requires no witness choice from an unproved existence assertion. The short exact sequence 0 -> B -> C -> A[0] -> 0 stays short exact after degree evaluation. In degree zero, a^0 is an isomorphism, so B^0=0. In every nonzero degree B^n -> C^n is an isomorphism because the third object is zero. Negative C terms vanish by the model predicate. If n>r, write n=q+1; an increasing embedding Fin(q+1) -> Fin r would imply q+1<=r, a contradiction, so the section product is an empty product and C^n=0. Hence B is supported in [1,r], including the empty interval when r=0.

Transport the term membership from Step 2 across B^n -> C^n for 1<=n<=r. Apply bounded_complex_mem_triangulated to B supported in [1,r]. This gives P(Q(B)), and shift closure gives P(Q(B)[1]). The short exact sequence of Step 3 gives a distinguished triangle Q(B) -> Q(C) -> Q(A[0]) -> Q(B)[1]. Rotate it once and compare with the standard cone triangle of a using identity isomorphisms on Q(C) and Q(A[0]). Mathlib isoTriangleOfIso12 supplies an isomorphism of the third vertices, so P(Q(Cone(a))).

The augmentation compatibility alpha.hom followed by Q(epsilon_K) = Q(a), with alpha:Q(C) ~= Q(K), identifies the first two vertices and first arrows of the two standard distinguished cone triangles. Mathlib isoTriangleOfIso12 extends these two isomorphisms to an isomorphism of triangles. Its third component transports P(Q(Cone(a))) to P(Q(Cone(epsilon_K))). No retract closure, K-flatness, orthogonality assumption or differential formula is used. Zero and nilpotent localization products, repeated generators and the empty generating list are included in the preceding argument.

theorem ringComplex_cech_cone_filtration
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)]
    (I : {I : Ideal A // I.FG})
    (K : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (εK : K ⟶ ringComplexSingle A)
    (hK : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val K εK)
    (P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules A)))
    [P.IsTriangulated] [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
    (hP : ∀ (s : A), s ∈ I.val → ∀ M : RingSiteModules A,
      Function.Bijective (fun x : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ↦ s • x) →
        P (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((HomologicalComplex.single (RingSiteModules A) (.up ℤ) 0).obj M))) :
    P (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone εK))
